topStories.headline: Glen Park's Bosworth Bridge Gets a Sky-Blue Makeover — and a Party to Match
topStories.dek: A years-long community art project has transformed a plain concrete span into a mosaic-covered landmark, with a public celebration set for September 26.
topStories.body:
Glen Park's Bosworth Pedestrian Bridge at Lippard Avenue has completed a dramatic transformation, emerging from a plain concrete span into what organizers call a first-of-its-kind tiled bridge in San Francisco. The bridge is now painted sky blue and features colorful mosaics on its pillars inspired by Indigenous patterns — the result of a collaboration between Glen Park Beautiful, the Department of Public Works, and students from the Glen Park School afterschool program.

The mosaic work was led by internationally recognized artist Ross Holzman, who guided Glen Park School students through the process of designing and installing the ceramic tile panels. Gardening volunteers also completed landscaping improvements surrounding the bridge. The project was organized by Glen Park Beautiful, with fiscal sponsorship from Independent Arts & Media and support from the Civic Joy Fund.

The Glen Park Association announced the transformation on September 12, inviting neighbors to a formal celebration on Saturday, September 26, from 1 to 3 p.m. at the Burnside mural and tiled steps at Burnside Street and Paradise Avenue — themselves a previous Glen Park Beautiful project. Reservations are requested.

The Bosworth Bridge project is the latest in a series of neighborhood beautification efforts in Glen Park that have included the Glen Park Greenway, the Burnside mural and tiled stairs, and the Elk Street mural.

topStories.headline: Planning Commission Unanimously Clears 29-Unit Condo Project at Former Eros Site on Market Street
topStories.dek: The San Francisco Planning Commission last week reapproved a 7-story, 29-unit mixed-use building at 2051 Market Street, the former site of the Castro's long-running gay club Eros, with modified plans.
topStories.body:
The San Francisco Planning Commission voted unanimously last week to reapprove a seven-story condominium building at 2051 Market Street, the former location of Eros, a gay sex club and sauna that operated in the Castro for roughly 30 years before closing. The vote, reported by Hoodline on September 8, clears a long-running project toward construction.

As currently approved with modifications, the building designed by Winder Gibson Architects will stand 85 feet tall and include 29 units — 15 one-bedroom and 14 two-bedroom market-rate condominiums — along with a 1,054-square-foot ground-floor retail space, a rooftop patio, and bike parking. Construction costs are estimated at $8 million.

The project has a lengthy history: it was originally submitted in 2022 by developer Shadi Aboukhater, who purchased the property in September 2020 for $3.6 million. The Planning Commission first approved it in June 2024, and the Department of Building Inspection issued a site permit in March 2025. The latest reapproval with modifications keeps the project on track toward breaking ground.

The Eros site sits near the intersection of Market Street and Safeway, along a stretch of upper Market that has seen a wave of new residential construction in recent years. The project is being developed by Aboukhater's firm Sak Design & Build.

topStories.headline: Two Castro Retail Fixtures Closing as September Ends — Fave and Entour Both Call It Quits
topStories.dek: A queer-owned screen-print shop and a 20-year-old men's clothing store are both shuttering by the end of September, adding to a string of recent Castro retail departures.
topStories.body:
Two longtime or recently established Castro businesses have announced they will close their doors by the end of September, underscoring ongoing pressure on brick-and-mortar retail in the neighborhood.

Fave, the queer mall and screen-print shop at 329 Noe Street, will close on September 26, less than three years after opening in April 2024 in the former Great Tan space. Owner Danae Lintz posted news of the closure in the store's window, citing insufficient foot traffic and rent that exceeded what sales could support. Lintz told Hoodline that screen-printing services will continue from a location on Treasure Island, and Fave merchandise will remain available online. A closing sale is underway through September 26; Fave Brand merchandise is not included.

Also closing at the end of September is Entour (2319 Market Street), a gay-owned men's clothing store that has operated in the Castro for 20 years. According to the Bay Area Reporter, the store cited financial pressure from federal tariffs as a contributing factor in the decision to close.

The two closures come as the Castro continues to navigate a mixed retail environment — Angela's Organic Ice Cream recently opened in a long-vacant storefront at 3998 18th Street, and the fully renovated Castro Theatre has been drawing crowds to the neighborhood since its February reopening.

events.title: Castro Night Market — Season Finale
events.description: The final Castro Night Market of 2026 takes over two blocks of 18th Street with local food vendors, merchants, live entertainment, and drag. The event is free; SFMTA will close 18th Street to traffic and reroute Muni lines during the event.

events.title: Glen Park Night Market — Final Market of 2026
events.location: Kern Street at Diamond, Glen Park
events.description: The fourth and final Glen Park Night Market of the summer brings local artists, artisan makers, live music, DJ sets, and family-friendly activities including face painting and kids' activities to Kern Street and its parking lot. Free admission; presented by the Glen Park Association, Glen Park Merchants Association, and ArtWalk SF.

events.title: Noe Valley Farmers Market
events.location: Noe Valley Town Square, 3861–3865 24th Street, Noe Valley
events.description: The year-round, volunteer-run certified farmers market on 24th Street offers fresh local produce and goods from regional farmers and producers, rain or shine.

events.title: Castro Farmers' Market
events.description: The weekly Castro Farmers' Market runs Wednesdays through November 18, 2026, with fresh produce and goods from regional farms and local vendors.

events.title: Bosworth Bridge Celebration
events.location: Burnside Street at Paradise Avenue, Glen Park
events.description: Glen Park Beautiful hosts a public celebration marking the completion of the Bosworth Pedestrian Bridge's transformation — now painted sky blue with mosaic pillars created by Glen Park School students. Reservations requested via the Glen Park Association website.

events.title: SF Good Neighbor Week Kickoff
events.location: Civic Center Plaza, San Francisco (citywide events through October 4)
events.description: San Francisco's second annual Good Neighbor Week launches with a free kickoff event at Civic Center Plaza featuring an opening ceremony, Good Neighbor Award recognition, neighborhood tables, live music, food trucks, and activities for all ages. Neighborhood events are scheduled across the city through October 4.
events.sourceName: SF Good Neighbor Week / Good Neighbor Lab

moreNews.headline: Angela's Organic Ice Cream Scoops Up Long-Vacant Castro Storefront
moreNews.body: Petaluma-based Angela's Organic Ice Cream opened a new Castro scoop shop at 3998 18th Street (at Noe), filling a storefront that had sat vacant after a planned specialty butcher shop abandoned its permitted space there, according to Hoodline (September 8). The shop is owned by Ignacio 'Iggy' Garat and his mother, Angela Pryor Garat, and specializes in small-batch ice cream and Latin-inspired flavors. Angela's already operates locations in Noe Valley and the Marina, as well as shops in Mill Valley, Healdsburg, and Petaluma.

moreNews.headline: Entour, 20-Year Castro Clothing Store, to Close by End of September
moreNews.body: Entour (2319 Market Street), a gay-owned men's clothing store that has been a Castro fixture for two decades, has announced it will close at the end of September 2026. The Bay Area Reporter noted the store cited financial pressures including the impact of federal tariffs on goods and shipping costs. The closure leaves another vacancy on the upper Market Street corridor.

restaurants.name: Frances
restaurants.description: Chef Melissa Perello's celebrated neighborhood restaurant serves a daily-changing menu of refined California cuisine with local, seasonal ingredients in a minimalist, welcoming dining room.

restaurants.name: Starbelly
restaurants.description: A casual Castro neighborhood favorite with a garden patio, serving forward-thinking California comfort food alongside craft cocktails, seasonal beer, and wine.

restaurants.name: Anchor Oyster Bar
restaurants.description: A Castro landmark since 1977, this intimate legacy seafood counter is renowned for its Michelin Bib Gourmand cioppino, fresh oysters, and sustainably sourced fish.

restaurants.name: Canela Bistro & Wine Bar
restaurants.description: A warm, LGBTQ+-owned bistro in the Castro serving Spanish tapas, shared plates, paella, and an inviting wine list in a candlelit space.

restaurants.name: Gada
restaurants.description: Opened in January 2026, this tiny Castro takeout spot builds all its sandwiches on house-made Tunisian malawi flatbread layered with freshly melted Swiss raclette cheese, harissa, and North African-inspired fillings.

restaurants.name: La Méditerranée
restaurants.description: A Castro neighborhood staple for decades, serving affordable mezze, Middle Eastern–inspired plates, and vegetarian-friendly Mediterranean comfort food.

restaurants.name: Wooden Spoon
restaurants.description: A cozy Duboce Triangle brunch spot serving American morning classics with occasional Scandinavian-inspired twists in a homey, welcoming space.

restaurants.name: Le Marais Bakery
restaurants.description: A Castro-area French bakery serving pastries, tartines, and weekend brunch in an airy space that transports diners to a Parisian neighborhood café.

restaurants.name: Willkommen
restaurants.description: An airy indoor beer garden on Upper Market pouring German-style beers from sister brewery Black Hammer, paired with bratwurst and hearty snacks.

restaurants.name: La Ciccia
restaurants.description: A beloved Noe Valley institution serving authentic Sardinian cuisine — handmade pasta, fresh seafood, and a deep all-Italian wine list — in an intimate, always-packed dining room.

restaurants.name: Firefly Restaurant
restaurants.description: A Noe Valley fixture for more than three decades, Firefly serves eclectic, globally inspired New American fare in a warm, art-filled dining room.

restaurants.name: Grand Lake Kitchen
restaurants.description: The East Bay fan favorite's new Noe Valley outpost offers all-day dining with two dog-friendly patios, a full bar, and a menu spanning brunch classics to dinner entrées.

restaurants.name: Gialina
restaurants.description: Widely regarded as one of San Francisco's best pizzerias, Gialina serves thin-crust pies with creative seasonal toppings in a lively Glen Park dining room.

restaurants.name: Canyon Market
restaurants.description: Glen Park's beloved family-owned full-service grocer stocks organic produce, in-house baked bread, prepared foods, a deli counter, and beer and wine — one block from Glen Park BART.

restaurants.name: Glen Park Station (The Station)
restaurants.description: Glen Park's go-to bar since 1926, serving adult beverages alongside live music and sports viewing in an atmosphere that epitomizes old San Francisco.

restaurants.name: Orphan Andy's
restaurants.description: A Castro institution open nearly around the clock, Orphan Andy's serves no-frills diner staples — burgers, eggs, and milkshakes — to the neighborhood at all hours.

restaurants.name: Pasta Panino
restaurants.description: A neighborhood counter in the Castro dishing up fresh pasta, Italian sandwiches, and daily specials at accessible prices.

restaurants.name: Fiorella Noe Valley
restaurants.description: Fiorella's Noe Valley location serves Neapolitan-style wood-fired pizzas, fresh handmade pastas, and a dozen spritz cocktails in a lively neighborhood setting.

hotels.name: Beck's Motor Lodge
hotels.description: A mid-century Castro motor lodge offering straightforward, affordable rooms in a prime location steps from the heart of the neighborhood.

hotels.name: Parker Guest House
hotels.description: An elegantly restored Edwardian inn with 21 rooms, a garden and sundeck, set on a quiet street just steps from the Castro's main commercial corridor.

hotels.name: Inn on Castro
hotels.description: A cozy, LGBTQ+-welcoming B&B in an Edwardian townhouse featuring individually decorated rooms, a communal breakfast, and a warm, personal atmosphere.

hotels.name: Willows Inn
hotels.description: A small, LGBTQ+-friendly inn offering European-style accommodations with shared baths and a welcoming atmosphere near Duboce Park.

hotels.name: Noe's Nest
hotels.description: A Victorian-era boutique B&B in Noe Valley praised by travelers as one of San Francisco's coziest and most characterful stays.

shops.name: Fabulosa Books
shops.description: A friendly Castro bookstore with a massive LGBTQ+ section, curated staff picks across literary fiction, history, and memoir, and a free book basket outside — winner of the Bay Area Reporter's Favorite Bookstore award three years running.

shops.name: Omnivore Books on Food
shops.description: The Bay Area's only dedicated culinary bookshop, stocking thousands of new and rare cookbooks and hosting author events with food luminaries from around the world.
shops.address: 3885A Cesar Chavez St, San Francisco, CA 94131

shops.name: Noe Valley Books
shops.description: Noe Valley's own independent bookstore, dedicated to providing books and services that spark humanity, joy, knowledge, and curiosity in the community and beyond.

shops.name: Bird & Beckett Books & Records
shops.description: Glen Park's beloved neighborhood bookstore and record shop on Chenery Street, known for its carefully curated selection and jazz-themed atmosphere.

shops.name: Perch
shops.description: A Glen Park shop easy to get lost in, stocking an eclectic mix of home goods, gifts, and accessories that reflect the neighborhood's creative spirit.

shops.name: Noe Valley Bakery
shops.description: A long-running Noe Valley bakery beloved for its blueberry pecan scones, artisan breads, and pastries that have earned it write-ups in the SF Bay Times.

shops.name: Cliff's Variety
shops.description: A Castro institution since 1936, Cliff's Variety is a beloved neighborhood hardware store stocking a vast and eclectic inventory of tools, supplies, costumes, and curiosities.

shops.name: Ambiance
shops.description: A locally owned women's boutique with multiple SF locations, offering an accessible mix of contemporary clothing, accessories, and shoes.

shops.name: Does Your Mother Know
shops.description: The Castro's cheeky, long-running gift shop carrying cards, novelties, art prints, and pride merchandise for every occasion.

shops.name: Harvest Urban Market
shops.description: A well-stocked Noe Valley neighborhood market carrying local and organic groceries, a curated wine selection, and ready-made foods.

artEntertainment.name: The Castro Theatre
artEntertainment.type: Historic cinema and live entertainment venue
artEntertainment.description: San Francisco's most celebrated movie palace, a 1922 Spanish Baroque Revival landmark that reopened in February 2026 after a $41 million renovation to host live concerts, comedy, film screenings, and community events.

artEntertainment.name: Harvey Milk Plaza
artEntertainment.description: The iconic public plaza at Market and Castro streets, anchored by a soaring rainbow flag and serving as a gathering place for marches, celebrations, and community events honoring LGBTQ+ history.
artEntertainment.address: Market St at Castro St, San Francisco, CA 94114

artEntertainment.name: GLBT Historical Society Museum
artEntertainment.description: The nation's only stand-alone museum dedicated to LGBTQ+ history, featuring rotating exhibitions on queer culture, activism, and community life in San Francisco and beyond.

artEntertainment.name: Fabulosa Books (Events)
artEntertainment.description: Beyond bookselling, Fabulosa Books hosts regular author readings, LGBTQ+ literary book clubs, and community conversations that have made it a cultural anchor of the Castro.

artEntertainment.name: Noe Valley Ministry
artEntertainment.description: A historic church building in Noe Valley that doubles as an intimate performance and community events space, hosting music concerts, film screenings, and neighborhood gatherings.

artEntertainment.name: Omnivore Books on Food (Events)
artEntertainment.description: Beyond its extraordinary cookbook collection, Omnivore regularly hosts author readings and book signings by the world's top food writers, chefs, and culinary historians.
artEntertainment.address: 3885A Cesar Chavez St, San Francisco, CA 94131

artEntertainment.name: Bird & Beckett Books & Records (Live Jazz)
artEntertainment.description: Glen Park's cultural gem hosts regular live jazz performances in its intimate shop space, blending a love of books with the neighborhood's thriving music culture.

artEntertainment.name: Qulture Collective
artEntertainment.type: Queer arts gallery and community space
artEntertainment.description: A Castro-area gallery and community arts space supporting LGBTQ+ visual artists through exhibitions, events, and programming rooted in queer culture.

gymsRecreation.name: Glen Canyon Park
gymsRecreation.type: Urban canyon park with trails and recreation center
gymsRecreation.description: One of San Francisco's best-kept natural secrets, Glen Canyon Park encompasses 70 acres of forested canyon with hiking trails, a recreation center offering baseball, tennis, basketball, pickleball, and the city's first public climbing wall.

gymsRecreation.name: Yoga Flow SF — Noe Valley
gymsRecreation.description: An all-levels heated vinyasa studio offering vigorous, athletic flow classes in a non-judgmental environment welcoming to beginners and advanced practitioners alike.

gymsRecreation.name: Beach Glass Hot Yoga & Pilates
gymsRecreation.description: A Noe Valley studio offering heated yoga and Pilates classes designed to build strength, flexibility, and endurance in a challenging, mindful environment.

gymsRecreation.name: Pure Barre Noe Valley
gymsRecreation.description: A Noe Valley outpost of the national barre brand, offering low-impact barre-inspired classes that blend strength training, flexibility, and Pilates-style movement.

gymsRecreation.name: Noe Valley Courts
gymsRecreation.description: A public recreation facility in Noe Valley featuring tennis courts and open space that has served as a community gathering and athletic hub for over 15 years.

gymsRecreation.name: Glen Park Recreation Center
gymsRecreation.description: A full-service SF Recreation and Parks facility at the foot of Glen Canyon offering baseball, tennis, basketball, pickleball, and the city's first public climbing wall, plus a year-round programming schedule.

gymsRecreation.name: Rikki Streicher Field (Upper Noe Recreation Center)
gymsRecreation.type: Public athletic field and recreation center
gymsRecreation.description: A beloved neighborhood athletic field and recreation center in Noe Valley serving as a hub for softball, community sports, and informal outdoor recreation.

gymsRecreation.name: Buena Vista Park
gymsRecreation.description: A densely forested hilltop park on the northern edge of Duboce Triangle, offering winding trails, panoramic city views, and off-leash dog areas.
gymsRecreation.address: Buena Vista Ave W, San Francisco, CA 94117

gymsRecreation.name: Duboce Park
gymsRecreation.type: Neighborhood park and off-leash dog area
gymsRecreation.description: A popular Duboce Triangle green space and one of SF's most beloved off-leash dog parks, surrounded by Victorian homes and served by Muni light rail.
gymsRecreation.address: Duboce Ave at Scott St, San Francisco, CA 94117

gymsRecreation.name: CORE40 Pilates
gymsRecreation.description: A Noe Valley–area studio delivering high-intensity reformer-inspired Pilates classes focused on strength, endurance, and full-body conditioning in a fast-paced environment.
